text.p: A bomb exploded in the Honduran Legislative Palace early Friday, shattering windows in the parliament and nearby buildings but causing no injuries, officials said.
"This explosive was high-powered," an officer of the army's bomb squad told Reuters. "It had a little more than five pounds (2.2 kg) of dynamite and a clock with a detonator."
Authorities said no one had claimed responsibility.
A similar bomb was deactivated outside the headquarters of the ruling Liberal Party, the officer said.
It was detected after a discotheque received an anonymous call saying that an explosive device had been placed at the offices of the Liberal Party of President Carlos Roberto Reina, he said.
The blast at the parliament building opened up a hole about 18 inches (45 cm) wide and broke windows at the neighboring Central Bank, a private bank and an office building.
